Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
257 AM EDT Fri Oct 9 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 254 AM EDT Friday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 254 AM EDT Friday...

1. Isolated to scattered showers today followed by a mostly dry 
weekend. 

2. The remnants of Isaias will bring periods of rain Sunday 
night into Monday morning but no significant impacts expected. 

3. Frontal system to bring next chances for showers on Monday 
night into Tuesday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 254 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper level low continues to build into the region 
today, bringing a couple more rounds of showers. The most widespread 
showers look to be in the afternoon and early evening as a broken 
line pushes down from the north. These will again be convective, and 
with temperatures aloft continuing to cool, a bit of graupel or pea 
sized hail will be possible out of the strongest showers. Shorter 
storms will make thunder unlikely, though it cannot be completely 
ruled out. Snow levels look to drop to around 4,000 feet before the 
precipitation exits this evening, so a couple flurries/snow showers 
are possible in the highest peaks. While hypothetical snow levels 
will continue to fall tonight, any sufficient moisture capable of 
producing precipitation will have exited, though a few lingering low 
clouds could produce rime ice. Surface high pressure builds into the 
region for tomorrow, leading to mostly sunny skies, lightening winds 
and high temperatures in the 50s for most places. Relatively 
widespread frost is likely tomorrow morning, but winds look to 
remain elevated for a longer portion of Friday night, so its extent 
in the Champlain looks somewhat limited and uncertain, though it 
could be enough for a Frost Advisory to be issued today. High 
pressure pushes to the east for Sunday and return southerly flow 
will cause temperatures to rise into the 60s. High clouds ahead of 
Isaias will infiltrate the region during the day.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The center of the remnants of Isaias will track well to 
our south Sunday night into Monday morning, but the precipitation 
shield will extend far north so showers and a period of stratiform 
rain are expected away from the international border. Totals ranging 
up to a half inch are currently expected, with the highest values 
farther south. There will likely be a sharp gradient on the northern 
end and where this exactly sets up remains uncertain. The rain 
should move out for most of the day monday though.

KEY MESSAGE 3: A low pressure system will track north of our forecast 
area, and a surface cold front drops south across our area on 
Tuesday. This front crossing the area brings our next chance for 
showers to the region. Following this frontal passage temperatures 
will trend below normal for a couple days.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...Mainly VFR conditions expected through 
the TAF period, with localized MVFR ceilings possible early 
Friday morning. Skies to remain FEW-SCT AOA 5000 ft through 08z.
Models then indicate low-level moisture will increase ahead of 
a weak surface trough moving south out of Canada 08z-14z Fri. 
Expect BKN-OVC ceilings 1500-2500 ft at SLK/EFK during this 
time, with lesser confidence at MPV. Elsewhere, ceilings will 
remain 4000+ ft. Clouds lift after 14z as mixing increases and 
MVFR will prevail thereafter. Additional scattered showers will 
develop again on Fri, but no visibility restrictions are 
expected. Winds will be light W/SW less than 8 kt overnight, 
trending a bit more NW and increasing to 6-10 kt with gusts to 
20 kt after 14z Fri. 

Outlook...

Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Columbus Day: MVFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Likely SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory is not in effect. However, a brief sharp 
increase in winds into the 25-35 KT range is possible in the 
afternoon as winds turn northerly behind a cold front. 

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
